Sound familiar?

Plenty of AI options. Not much clarity on what comes next.

Every leadership team has been told AI will change how they work. Most have tried a pilot or two, and most already pay for platforms with AI built in. The harder part is turning all of that into results the business can count on. Whatever your industry, it usually comes down to four things.

Almost everyone is using AI. Far fewer are seeing it pay off.

88%

of organisations now use AI in at least one part of the business — McKinsey, 2025

16%

have scaled their AI initiatives across the enterprise — IBM, 2025

25%

of AI initiatives have delivered the return CEOs expected — IBM, 2025

42%

of companies scrapped most of their AI initiatives in 2025, up from 17% a year earlier — S&P Global, 2025

Card 1 · Prioritising

“Where do we start?” So many processes could use AI, and every one has a champion. Without a clear way to rank them, the most valuable work waits while the loudest request moves first. The cost: effort spreads thin. Gartner expected at least 30% of generative AI projects to be abandoned after proof of concept by the end of 2025, with unclear business value among the reasons.

Card 2 · Scaling

“The pilot worked. Now what?” A promising demo is a long way from something hundreds of people rely on. Security, integrations and ownership all need answers before it can grow. The cost: good ideas stall. The average company scraps 46% of its AI proofs of concept before they reach production.

Card 3 · Time to value

“When will we see a return?” Long programmes ask for patience before anyone sees a number. Meanwhile the hours and the money keep slipping. The cost: momentum fades. 60% of senior leaders outside the C-suite expect scaling barriers to take a year or more to clear.

Card 4 · Aligning with business outcomes

“Is this moving what matters?” AI goals and business goals drift apart easily. Activity gets measured, results don’t, and the next step gets harder to justify. The cost: spend without a story. Half of CEOs say the pace of AI investment has left them with disconnected technology, and only 39% of organisations see any EBIT impact from AI.

If any of these sound like your week, you’re in good company. They’re the reason Simpliigence AI exists.

Every quarter a process stays manual, it costs you twice.

Once in hours and margin, and again in the good people who spend their week on work a well-built agent could handle. Closing that gap doesn’t take a big programme. It takes one process, done properly, with a number attached. That’s where we start.

The real decision

A sea of choices makes the next step harder, not easier.

Every platform has an AI story, every vendor has a roadmap, and models improve every quarter. Choosing well asks you to make three big calls before you’ve seen a single result. That’s a lot to carry on your own.

Which platform to commit to

Claude, Copilot, Agentforce and OpenAI are all strong at different things, and the right one depends on where your data lives and what you already license.

How much to fund up front

Most AI work is scoped in hours and paid before anyone knows what it will return.

Who looks after it once it’s live

Models change every quarter, and an agent needs someone who owns it long after the project team moves on.

Each of these is a fair question. We built our whole model around answering them before you commit.

The good news

It’s working for nearly half of companies. Here’s what they do.

Nearly half of companies are now creating real value from AI, and the most advanced see 2.4 times the revenue growth of those still waiting. What sets them apart isn’t a bigger budget. It’s the order they work in.

They start with where the value is

Clarity on which processes matter comes before any choice of tool.

They reshape the work, not just the software

High performers are nearly three times as likely to have redesigned their workflows end to end.

They build governance in from the start

Security, approvals and ownership travel with the AI, so it can grow.

They measure it in the numbers

Impact shows up in the P&L, not just in activity reports.

That’s the approach we built Simpliigence AI around.

Why Simpliigence AI

Outcomes, by design. Here’s what that means for you.

We’ve spent six years delivering Salesforce, data and automation for more than 125 companies. Again and again, we met strong teams stuck at the same point: plenty of options, no clear next step, and real pressure to show results. We created Simpliigence AI to help them prioritise, scale, see value sooner and keep AI tied to business outcomes, using the tools they already have.

The outcome comes first

We agree the number before we choose a model, a tool or a timeline.

The design fits you

Your platform, your data, your screens and your security rules shape the build.

We stay accountable

We’re paid when the result shows up, and we keep running what we build.

That’s the order we work in. First the result, then the design that gets you there.

Wherever you’re starting, there’s a way in.

Prioritising

More places AI could go than time to try them. A half-day AI Health Check ranks your processes by value and names the KPI each would move. What changes: your effort goes to the two or three processes worth the most.

Scaling

Pilots that stall before production. Every build is designed for production from the first sprint: human approval, an audit trail, your trust boundary, a named owner. Then we run it. What changes: the pilot becomes part of the working day.

Time to value

A long wait before anyone sees a return. A working pilot on your real data in five to eight weeks. AgentBox agents set up in as little as 10 days. What changes: a measured result in weeks, not quarters.

Alignment

AI drifting away from business goals. One KPI agreed before work starts, our fees tied to it, and a monthly ROI report. What changes: every agent is tied to a number the business already cares about.

Existing spend

Licences already paid for. We build on the Claude, Copilot or Agentforce you have, and the logic ports when models improve. What changes: value from what you own, with no new platform to buy.

Guides

Each guide is a short page (500 to 800 words) that opens with a two-sentence direct answer, then goes deeper. These are the pages AI search tools quote.

An AI automation platform is the layer that lets AI read business data, decide the next step and act across your systems. It differs from traditional automation because it handles exceptions and changing inputs instead of breaking on them.
An AI model reads a request or record, pulls the context it needs from your systems, and proposes or takes the next action. A person approves anything that matters until the agent has proved its accuracy on your own data.
Start with one process that repeats and costs time. Map it, remove the waste, then let an agent handle the steps that need judgment and a workflow tool handle the ones that don’t.

Company

An AI-first company with six years of delivery behind it.

Simpliigence AI was built to do one thing well: put AI agents to work and stand behind the result. We bring the depth of Simpliigence with us.

Our story

Simpliigence has spent six years helping more than 125 companies get more from Salesforce, data and automation. Along the way, clients started asking for something different: not another pilot, but agents that run every day and a partner willing to be measured on them. Simpliigence AI is our answer. We test everything on ourselves first. In four months we built eight internal apps with Claude and retired five SaaS tools.

What we believe

Outcomes over hours

If we can’t name the number, we shouldn’t start.

Your stack, not ours

The best AI is the one that fits what you already run.

People stay in charge

Agents propose, people approve, until trust is earned.

We stay after go-live

Every agent has a named owner, long after launch.

One team. Three time zones. One number to hit.

Follow the sun

One accountable team across New Jersey, Toronto, London, the Netherlands and Bangalore. That’s 18.5 hours of cover a day, with two live handovers.

AI drafts, a person approves

AI drafts every delivery artefact, from discovery notes to code. A person reviews before anything reaches your systems.

Accepted on the numbers

Golden datasets and hit-rate measurement, so progress is a fact on a dashboard.

Run after go-live
